# LBTech IoT Cloud & Micro-Container Platform
> Documentation and Machine-Readable Context for Large Language Models (LLMs) & AI Agents

## 1. System Overview
LBTech IoT Cloud Platform is a dedicated academic IoT infrastructure developed for Computer Technology students at Lopburi Technical College (วิทยาลัยเทคนิคลพบุรี). It provides each student group with isolated cloud containers, time-series telemetry storage, MQTT broker connectivity, and edge micro-controller integrations.

- Official Portal URL: https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io
- Machine Context / LLM Docs: https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/llms.txt
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) Endpoint: https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/api/mcp

---

## 2. Platform Architecture & Service Endpoints

### 2.1 MQTT Broker (EMQX v5.8 Enterprise Cluster)
- Broker Host (WebSocket WSS): `mqtt.pichyy.qzz.io`
- WSS Port & Path: Port `443` / Path `/mqtt` (TLS/SSL encrypted via Cloudflare)
- Broker Host (Native TCP): `mqtt.pichyy.qzz.io` or `techniccom.tail59415d.ts.net` (Port `1883`)
- Username: Student ID (e.g. `69123456789`)
- Password: Group Student Password
- Student Topic Namespace:
  - Telemetry Upload: `project/{studentId}/sensor`
  - Actuator / Relay Control: `project/{studentId}/control`
  - Broadcast Status: `project/{studentId}/status`
  - Subscribe Pattern: `project/{studentId}/#`

### 2.2 Time-Series Database (InfluxDB v2.7)
- Web UI & Flux Data Explorer: https://influx.pichyy.qzz.io
- InfluxDB API Endpoint: `https://influx.pichyy.qzz.io` (or `https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/api/v2`)
- Organization (Org): `lbtech`
- Default Bucket: `telemetry-{studentId}` (or `iot-telemetry`)
- Retention Policy: 30 days automatic retention
- Authentication: API Token passed in HTTP Header `Authorization: Token {influxToken}`
- Write Protocol: InfluxDB Line Protocol via POST `/api/v2/write?org=lbtech&bucket=telemetry-{studentId}&precision=s`
  Format: `sensor,student_id={studentId},device=esp32 temperature=28.5,humidity=65.2`

### 2.3 Cloud Micro-Containers (Dedicated Linux CT)
- Container Engine: Docker on Proxmox VE (Debian 12 Bookworm, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Alpine Linux 3.22)
- Storage: Persistent bind mount at `/workspace` (Files are preserved across container reboots)
- Resource Allocation: 1-2 vCPU, 512-2048 MB RAM, 5-10 GB SSD Quota
- Root Access: Full sudo/root access inside container (`root`)
- In-Browser Web Console: Integrated xterm.js terminal with direct PTY WebSocket (`wss://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/api/ct/terminal/{vmid}`)
- External SSH Bastion Jump Host:
  - Command: `ssh {studentId}@techniccom.tail59415d.ts.net -p 10000`
  - Compatible with VS Code Remote - SSH extension.

### 2.4 REST API & Webhooks
- Telemetry Write (JSON): POST `https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/api/telemetry/write`
  Headers: `Content-Type: application/json`
  Body: `{"studentId": "...", "temperature": 28.5, "humidity": 60}`
- Telemetry Query (Flux): POST `https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/api/telemetry/query`
- Server Management:
  - Power On: POST `https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/api/ct/servers/{vmid}/power` (`action: "start"`)
  - Power Off: POST `https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/api/ct/servers/{vmid}/power` (`action: "stop"`)
  - Reboot: POST `https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/api/ct/servers/{vmid}/reboot`
  - Real-Time Stats (SSE): GET `https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/api/ct/servers/{vmid}/stats/stream`

## 3. Recommended Code Implementations for Micro-controllers

### 3.1 ESP32 (Arduino C++ via PubSubClient & WiFiClientSecure)
```cpp
#include <WiFi.h>
#include <PubSubClient.h>

const char* ssid = "YOUR_WIFI_SSID";
const char* password = "YOUR_WIFI_PASS";

const char* mqtt_server = "mqtt.pichyy.qzz.io";
const int mqtt_port = 1883;
const char* mqtt_user = "YOUR_STUDENT_ID";
const char* mqtt_pass = "YOUR_PASSWORD";
const char* topic_pub = "project/YOUR_STUDENT_ID/sensor";

WiFiClient espClient;
PubSubClient client(espClient);

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  WiFi.begin(ssid, password);
  while (WiFi.status() != WL_CONNECTED) { delay(500); }
  client.setServer(mqtt_server, mqtt_port);
}

void loop() {
  if (!client.connected()) {
    client.connect("ESP32_Client", mqtt_user, mqtt_pass);
  }
  client.loop();
  // Example payload: {"temp": 28.4, "humi": 65.0}
  String payload = "{\"temperature\":28.4,\"humidity\":65.0}";
  client.publish(topic_pub, payload.c_str());
  delay(5000);
}
```

### 3.2 Python MQTT & InfluxDB Client (Running inside Container)
```python
import time
import json
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt
from influxdb_client import InfluxDBClient, Point
from influxdb_client.client.write_api import SYNCHRONOUS

STUDENT_ID = "YOUR_STUDENT_ID"
INFLUX_URL = "https://influx.pichyy.qzz.io"
INFLUX_TOKEN = "YOUR_INFLUX_TOKEN"
INFLUX_ORG = "lbtech"
INFLUX_BUCKET = f"telemetry-{STUDENT_ID}"

influx = InfluxDBClient(url=INFLUX_URL, token=INFLUX_TOKEN, org=INFLUX_ORG)
write_api = influx.write_api(write_options=SYNCHRONOUS)

def on_message(client, userdata, msg):
    data = json.loads(msg.payload.decode())
    point = Point("sensor") \
        .tag("student_id", STUDENT_ID) \
        .field("temperature", float(data.get("temp", 0))) \
        .field("humidity", float(data.get("humi", 0)))
    write_api.write(bucket=INFLUX_BUCKET, record=point)
    print("Logged to InfluxDB:", data)

client = mqtt.Client(client_id=f"python_{STUDENT_ID}")
client.username_pw_set(STUDENT_ID, "YOUR_PASSWORD")
client.on_message = on_message
client.connect("mqtt.pichyy.qzz.io", 1883, 60)
client.subscribe(f"project/{STUDENT_ID}/#")
client.loop_forever()
```

## 4. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration
AI coding assistants (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Antigravity) can connect directly to LBTech IoT Platform via the MCP JSON-RPC protocol:
- MCP Server URL: `https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/api/mcp`
- Claude Desktop Config:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lbtech-iot": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch", "https://iot.pichyy.qzz.io/api/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```
